items.title: Iran envoy deletes post on Islamabad delegation amid ceasefire rift

featured_image.name: What to Know About Iran’s Ceasefire Proposal as Peace Talks Approach

items.description:
Iran's Ambassador to Pakistan, Reza Amiri Moghadam, deleted a post on X late Thursday announcing that an Iranian delegation would arrive in Islamabad that evening for talks with the United States, raising fresh uncertainty about whether high-stakes negotiations set for Friday will go ahead as planned.

Moghadam had written that "despite skepticism of Iranian public opinion due to repeated ceasefire violations by Israeli regime to sabotage the diplomatic initiative," the delegation would arrive Thursday night at the invitation of Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for "serious talks based on 10 points proposed by Iran," according to Moneycontrol, which published the text of the post before it was removed. The post was subsequently deleted, Xinhua International reported, though no official explanation was given.[1][2]

items.title: Iran demands Bitcoin tolls for Hormuz tanker passage

featured_image.name: Oil Tanker Collision Near Strait of Hormuz Raises Security ...

items.description: Despite a two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran announced Tuesday evening, Tehran is pressing ahead with demands that oil tankers pay tolls in Bitcoin and other digital currencies to transit the Strait of Hormuz, raising doubts about whether the critical waterway will see a meaningful return of commercial shipping anytime soon.

items.title: UK forces Russian submarines to retreat from undersea cables

featured_image.name: MPs warned Russia is way ahead in undersea warfare

items.description:
Britain on Thursday revealed it had tracked three Russian submarines conducting covert operations near undersea cables and pipelines in waters north of the UK, in a month-long surveillance campaign that ended with all three vessels retreating toward Russia.

Defence Secretary John Healey said British forces identified an Akula-class nuclear attack submarine entering international waters in the High North several weeks ago and quickly determined it was deployed as a distraction while two submarines from Russia's Main Directorate of Deep Sea Research, known as GUGI, carried out what the Ministry of Defence described as "nefarious activity" near critical underwater infrastructure.[1]

items.title: Iran's nuclear chief rejects enrichment curbs ahead of Islamabad talks

featured_image.name: Iran's atomic chief says uranium enrichment Teheran's red line

items.description:
Iran's nuclear chief Mohammad Eslami on Thursday dismissed demands to curtail the country's uranium enrichment program, calling such efforts futile just days before high-stakes negotiations with the United States are set to begin in Pakistan's capital.

Speaking on the sidelines of a memorial service marking 40 days since the death of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Eslami said that "the claims and demands of our enemies to restrict Iran's enrichment programme are merely wishes that will be buried," according to Iran's ISNA news agency. He added that no law or external pressure could halt Iran's nuclear progress and that demands to abandon enrichment were "nonsensical".[1][2][3]

items.title: Netanyahu orders direct peace talks with Lebanon on Hezbollah

featured_image.name: Netanyahu agrees to join Trump’s Gaza Board of Peace after initial pushback

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced Thursday that he had instructed his cabinet to begin direct negotiations with Lebanon "as soon as possible," a move that marks a reversal after Israel previously rebuffed Lebanese overtures for talks.[1][2]

"In light of Lebanon's repeated requests to open direct negotiations with Israel, I instructed the cabinet yesterday to start direct negotiations with Lebanon as soon as possible," Netanyahu said in a statement, according to Reuters. The negotiations would focus on "disarming Hezbollah and establishing peaceful relations between Israel and Lebanon," he added.[3][1]

items.title: Trump demands European warships in Hormuz within days

featured_image.name: Trump claims coalition to send war ships to reopen strait of Hormuz

items.description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is insisting that any German military involvement in securing the Strait of Hormuz must come under an international mandate, setting up a diplomatic standoff with President Donald Trump, who has issued what European diplomats describe as an ultimatum demanding allied warships in the waterway within days.

items.title: Oil prices climb again as Strait of Hormuz stays shut despite ceasefire

featured_image.name: Iran confirms seizure of oil tanker in the Strait of Hormuz

items.description: The two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran, announced on April 7, has done little to settle global energy and commodity markets, as the Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed and oil prices have begun climbing again after an initial sharp selloff.

items.title: Finland nears launch of world's first permanent nuclear waste site

featured_image.name: Finland's plan to bury spent nuclear fuel for 100,000 years

items.description: After more than two decades of construction, Finland's Onkalo facility is set to become the first site on Earth to permanently dispose of spent nuclear fuel, with authorities expected to grant an operating license within months, according to the Associated Press.[1]

items.title: US-Iran ceasefire teeters as Israel bombs Beirut, Hormuz stays blocked

featured_image.name: Ceasefire Reaction And U.S.Israeli Military Campaign In Iran

items.description:
A fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran, brokered through last-minute Pakistani mediation, was teetering by its second day on Thursday amid disputes over whether Lebanon is covered by the truce and whether the Strait of Hormuz has truly reopened.

The Associated Press reported Thursday that the ceasefire was "overwhelmed by Israel's heavy bombardment of Beirut, Iran's ongoing grip on the Strait of Hormuz, and doubts regarding whether negotiators can bridge a myriad of other disparities."[1]

items.title: OpenAI pauses Stargate UK data center over energy costs

featured_image.name: OpenAI's flagship UK data project delayed in setback for Starmer

items.description: OpenAI announced on Thursday that it is pausing its Stargate artificial intelligence infrastructure project in the United Kingdom, pointing to the high cost of energy and an uncertain regulatory environment as key obstacles to moving forward. The decision deals a blow to the British government's strategy of positioning AI as a driver of economic growth.[1][2]

items.title: Iran war doubles Russia's oil tax revenue to $9 bn in April

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Iran war doubles Russia's main oil revenue to $9 bln in April,  Reuters calculations show | Reuters

items.description: Russia's revenue from its largest single oil tax is on course to double in April to around $9 billion, according to Reuters calculations published on Thursday, as the global energy crisis triggered by the US and Israeli military campaign against Iran delivers an unexpected financial lifeline to Moscow.[1][2][3]

items.title: Earth grew 16% brighter at night since 2014, study finds

featured_image.name: Nighttime Lights Map of Earth Shows Changes Over Past Decade

items.description: Earth's nighttime glow increased by a net 16 percent between 2014 and 2022, according to a study published Wednesday in the journal Nature that also revealed the planet's artificial lighting is far more volatile than scientists previously understood.[1][2]

items.title: UK's Cooper demands toll-free Strait of Hormuz passage

featured_image.name: Britain to call for toll-free Strait of Hormuz amid US-Iran ceasefire

items.description:
British Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper is set to declare on Thursday that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz must remain free of tolls, directly challenging both Iran's efforts to control the waterway and a suggestion from President Donald Trump to establish a joint toll system for the critical passage.[1][2]

In her annual foreign policy address at Mansion House in London, Cooper will argue that international maritime law forbids levying charges on vessels transiting the strait, which carries roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas.[3][4]

"The fundamental freedoms of the seas must not be unilaterally withdrawn or sold off to individual bidders. Nor can there be any place for tolls on an international waterway. Freedom of navigation means navigation must be free," Cooper will say, according to advance excerpts of the speech.[4][2]

items.title: Chevron projects up to $2.2B Q1 earnings boost from higher oil prices

featured_image.name: Chevron CEO says Iran war impact isn't fully priced into oil market

items.description:
Chevron said on Thursday that higher commodity prices driven by the war in Iran are expected to lift its first-quarter upstream earnings by $1.6 billion to $2.2 billion compared with the fourth quarter of 2025, even as the conflict cut into the company's global production.[1][2]

The disclosure, made in a regulatory filing, comes a day after rival Exxon Mobil issued a similar update showing the Iran war's dual impact on the world's largest oil producers: surging prices that pad upstream profits, offset by physical disruptions to output across the Persian Gulf.[3][4]

items.title: Meta expands CoreWeave deal to $21B, launches Muse Spark AI model

featured_image.name: Meta debuts new AI model, attempting to catch up to Google, OpenAI

items.description: Meta Platforms made a pair of moves this week to accelerate its artificial intelligence ambitions, launching a new flagship AI model called Muse Spark on Wednesday and announcing a $21 billion cloud computing agreement with CoreWeave on Thursday.

items.title: IUCN lists emperor penguins as endangered over sea ice loss

featured_image.name: Accidental discovery reveals new climate threat to emperor penguins

items.description: The International Union for Conservation of Nature has officially listed emperor penguins as endangered on its Red List of Threatened Species, elevating the iconic Antarctic birds from their previous classification of "near threatened" in a move driven by climate-fueled sea ice loss. The update, announced Thursday, marks one of the most dramatic reclassifications for a polar species in recent years.[1][2]

items.title: New model suggests dark matter has two particle states

featured_image.name: Fermilab scientists to look for dark matter using quantum ...

items.description: A team of physicists has put forward a new framework suggesting dark matter may consist of two distinct particle states rather than one, offering a potential explanation for why gamma-ray signals observed at the center of the Milky Way have not appeared in smaller nearby galaxies. The paper, titled "dSph-obic dark matter," was published on Wednesday in the Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics by Asher Berlin, Joshua Foster, Dan Hooper, and Gordan Krnjaic, all affiliated with the Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory.[1][2]

items.title: Goldman Sachs cuts gas forecast after ceasefire but warns risks remain

featured_image.name: Natural gas, LNG prices soar on Middle East supply fears - CNBC

items.description: Goldman Sachs has warned that global natural gas markets face a prolonged supply shock stemming from Iranian attacks on Qatar's liquefied natural gas infrastructure, even as a fragile two-week ceasefire between the United States and Iran offers temporary relief. The bank said in an April 2 research note that European gas prices could surge to 75–100 euros per megawatt-hour — roughly double recent levels — if disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz persist beyond April.[1]

items.title: Oil surges past $97 as Iran re-closes Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: Oil prices rise again and Asian stocks retreat on the fragile Iran ...

items.description: Oil prices climbed back above $97 a barrel on Thursday and Asian stocks retreated as optimism over a fragile U.S.-Iran ceasefire gave way to renewed uncertainty, after Israel launched its largest coordinated strike in Lebanon and Iran moved to re-close the Strait of Hormuz.[1][2]

items.title: Dow surges over 1,300 points after U.S.-Iran ceasefire

featured_image.name: Stock market news for April 8, 2026 - CNBC

items.description: U.S. stocks surged on Wednesday in their best session in a year after the United States and Iran agreed to a two-week ceasefire, raising hopes that a crippling oil shortage could begin to ease. The Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 1,325 points, or 2.85%, while the S&P 500 climbed 2.5% and the Nasdaq Composite rose as much as 3.5%. It was the Dow's largest single-day gain since April 2025, when markets rallied after a tariff pause.[1][2][3]
